policy: Display tuning never fabricates capability. Only documented Win32 interfaces are used (EnumDisplayDevices, EnumDisplaySettings, ChangeDisplaySettingsEx, Get/SetDeviceGammaRamp, dxva2 physical monitor queries). GPU-vendor saturation controls (Digital Vibrance, AMD Saturation, Intel color) are not writable through documented APIs here, so they are offered as manual instructions only. Gamma ramps are applied ABSOLUTELY from a captured original, never relative to the current ramp, so repeated applies cannot accumulate into a green or oversaturated image. No GPU registry value is ever written.

safety.defaultVibranceGuidance: Vendor saturation controls default to 50 percent on NVIDIA Digital Vibrance. Raise it in small steps (5 percent) if you choose; never start at maximum.

profiles.name: Platinum Competitive
profiles.purpose: A conservative visibility lift for competitive play: a small, bounded gamma lift and optional highest-available refresh on the SELECTED display only.
profiles.scope: Selected display only. Changes the GPU output gamma ramp for that display; it is not per-game and affects the whole desktop until restored.
profiles.vibranceGuidance: Optional, manual only: NVIDIA Control Panel > Digital Vibrance or AMD Display > Saturation. Increase by 5-10 percent at most; verify skin tones and map colors before keeping it.
tradeoffs: A gamma lift reduces shadow depth; colors are slightly washed out versus the calibrated state.
Refresh change may reset some fullscreen game modes once.

profiles.name: CS2 Visibility
profiles.purpose: Brighten dark corners modestly for Counter-Strike 2 without crushing highlights.
profiles.scope: Selected display gamma ramp. Global for the desktop while active. CS2 itself has no brightness API that external tools may touch; in-game Brightness/Contrast remain the per-game control.
profiles.vibranceGuidance: CS2 pros often raise Digital Vibrance 10-20 percent manually. Do it in the NVIDIA/AMD control panel, not here; start low and compare wall and skin colors.
tradeoffs: If CS2 runs exclusive fullscreen it may bypass the desktop gamma ramp; test in the actual mode you play.

profiles.name: Fortnite Visibility
profiles.purpose: Slight gamma lift for Fortnite's already bright art style; useful mainly in Performance mode where shadows are minimal.
profiles.scope: Selected display gamma ramp, global for the desktop while active.
profiles.vibranceGuidance: Fortnite colors are already saturated; raising vendor saturation usually oversaturates. Consider leaving it at default.
tradeoffs: Fortnite DX12 mode with Lumen ignores simple gamma expectations; compare in a real match, not the lobby.

profiles.name: Rust Visibility
profiles.purpose: Modest lift for Rust's dark interiors and night cycle.
profiles.scope: Selected display gamma ramp, global for the desktop while active.
profiles.vibranceGuidance: Manual only, small steps. Rust night scenes clip quickly if gamma and saturation are both raised.
tradeoffs: Daylight scenes will look washed out while the profile is active; restore when finished.

profiles.name: Natural Colors
profiles.purpose: Return the selected display to a neutral ramp (identity gamma) while keeping the captured original restorable.
profiles.vibranceGuidance: If you previously raised vendor saturation, reset it to default in the GPU control panel.
tradeoffs: None; identity ramp is what Windows starts with.

profiles.name: Movie & Media
profiles.purpose: Slightly deeper contrast curve for film playback.
profiles.vibranceGuidance: Leave saturation at default; media players and video drivers apply their own color processing.

profiles.name: HDR Gaming
profiles.purpose: Does NOT write any HDR setting. It checks what can be detected and opens Windows HDR settings, because HDR enablement and tone mapping are user-facing and panel-dependent.
profiles.scope: Guidance only plus a shortcut to Settings > Display > HDR.
profiles.vibranceGuidance: Under HDR, desktop gamma ramps are typically ignored; vendor saturation controls may behave differently. Do not combine a gamma profile with HDR and judge the result from SDR screenshots.
tradeoffs: HDR appearance depends on panel peak brightness; on low-brightness panels SDR may look better.

profiles.name: Color-Accurate / Creator
profiles.purpose: Identity ramp, no refresh change, and guidance to use Windows Color Management (ICC profile) instead of GPU tweaks.
profiles.scope: Selected display gamma ramp set to identity.
profiles.vibranceGuidance: Reset any vendor saturation to default. Load your monitor's ICC profile via colorcpl.exe if the manufacturer provides one.
tradeoffs: Games may look less punchy than with saturation boosts.

profiles.name: Restore Previous Display Configuration
profiles.purpose: Restores the resolution, refresh rate, and gamma ramp captured before the first Platinum display change on the selected display.
profiles.vibranceGuidance: Vendor saturation changes made manually in the GPU control panel must be reverted there; Platinum Optimizer never wrote them.

gameNotes.cs2: CS2 offers in-game Brightness, Contrast, and an HRTF audio option. Global Windows/GPU color changes cannot be limited to CS2 alone; the selected technology here (desktop gamma ramp) is global by nature.
gameNotes.fortnite: Fortnite has no external color API; use in-game Brightness and Display Mode. Global ramp changes affect the desktop, not just Fortnite.
gameNotes.rust: Rust has an in-game brightness slider; global ramp changes are not per-game. No game memory or anti-cheat interaction is performed.
